what: Time from navigation (commit) until the chapter model is on screen, in ms, on this laptop over loopback, headless Chromium (Playwright 1.56.0) at 1440×900. 'cold' is the first load of the chapter in a fresh browser context; 'warm' the second and third. 'explorerToModel' is the exchange suite's step 9: on Chapter 8, switch to the connected explorer, reload, then click back to the chapter model. One run of each variant, three navigations; the numbers are noisy by a few hundred ms and are read for their direction, not their decimals.

baseline.source: commit e4162e6 (v20.4): Cache-Control: no-store, no preloading

baseline2.source: the same, run again after the others

B_revalidation_only.source: ETag + Cache-Control: no-cache (304 when unchanged), no preloading

D_preload_only.source: no-store as before, plus modulepreload of the page's closure in index.html and of a chapter view's closure alongside its import

C_both.source: the tests commit 951edae: revalidation and preloading together

reading: Revalidation alone (B) is neutral on loopback: within the noise of the baseline on every measure.

Preloading (D, and C) is slower on loopback: the explorer-to-model switch doubles (about 1 s against about 0.45 s) and warm loads grow. The burst of parallel requests competes with the import's own chain, and loopback has no latency for the preload to hide.

Neither change shortens the 2–3 s a warm navigation takes to show a model: that time is the page's own boot, compile and render of about 5.6 MB of unbundled modules, not the network. A bundle is the lever, and is not part of this release.
shipped: Revalidation (ETag + no-cache) and the loading placeholder. Preloading is not shipped. Revalidation's benefit is expected on a network, where the modules would otherwise travel on every navigation; it is reasoned, not measured here.
